_comment: Experience budgets for the installable PWA (apps/web). Perceived latency only — byte and request ceilings live in apps/web/tests/e2e/perf-budgets.ts. See README.md in this directory for the status vocabulary and the year-3 volume table. Ratcheted tighten-only via PERF_BUDGET_SOURCES.

coldOpenToUsable.probe: apps/web/tests/e2e/perf-waterfall.spec.ts — 'web vitals — LCP / INP / CLS on a cold shell load'
coldOpenToUsable._note: Blocked on the same missing first-contentful-paint as largestContentfulPaint. What IS observable in this harness today (2026-07-31 run): domContentLoadedEventEnd 32-52 ms, loadEventEnd 48-96 ms, first-paint 44 ms. Those are document-lifecycle events, not 'first usable screen', so they are recorded here as context and NOT promoted to a ceiling. perfBudgets.timing.coldOpenMsSoftCeiling (15,000 ms, enforceTiming === true) is the machine-cost twin that gates today.

largestContentfulPaint.probe: apps/web/tests/e2e/perf-waterfall.spec.ts — 'web vitals (LCP/INP/CLS) on a cold shell load'

_provenance.attempted: 2026-07-31, darwin arm64, Playwright bundled headless Chromium, apps/web e2e harness
_provenance.result: NO LCP ENTRY. The probe ran, all three observers installed (`installed: [largest-contentful-paint, layout-shift, event]`), the connect screen rendered fully (accessibility snapshot shows heading + ticket field), and the paint timeline contained ONLY `first-paint=44` — no `first-contentful-paint`, hence no LCP candidate, after 16 s.
_provenance.note: The ceiling is deliberately parked in `_intendedCeilingMs` (underscore = invisible to the ratchet) rather than shipped as `ceilingMs`. Shipping the Core Web Vitals 2500 ms threshold as a live ceiling would gate on a value the browser never emits, which passes vacuously forever. First suspect for the missing FCP: shell content that is not yet a contentful paint to the compositor (webfont with font-display: block, or an opacity/transition that never resolves in this harness). Promote to `ceilingMs` the moment a run produces a number.

interactionToNextPaint.probe: apps/web/tests/e2e/perf-waterfall.spec.ts — 'web vitals (LCP/INP/CLS) on a cold shell load'

_provenance.result: NO EVENT-TIMING ENTRY. The cold connect screen exposes no visible button, so the probe's deliberate click timed out (`interactionDriven: false`) and Chromium recorded no interaction. INP is undefined without one.
_provenance.note: Parked in `_intendedCeilingMs` for the same reason as LCP. Closing this needs the probe to interact with a control that exists on the cold screen — the pairing-ticket textbox is present; a keypress-driven INP capture is the obvious next step and does not need any apps/web/src change.

cumulativeLayoutShift.probe: apps/web/tests/e2e/perf-waterfall.spec.ts — 'web vitals (LCP/INP/CLS) on a cold shell load'

_provenance.host: darwin arm64, Playwright bundled headless Chromium, apps/web e2e harness
_provenance.note: MEASURED and HARD-GATED — the one vital this harness produces honestly, and the only one of the three currently asserted. Observed 0 (no unexpected layout shift on the cold connect screen). The ceiling is the Core Web Vitals 'good' threshold rather than observed+headroom, because a 0 + headroom ceiling would be 0 and any first honest shift would red the lane; 0.1 is the point at which a user notices.

appWeight.probe: scripts/perf/app-weight.mjs --surface web (weighs apps/web/dist produced by `bun run web:build`), run in CI after the web build

_provenance.host: linux x64 worktree, `bun run --cwd apps/web build` (vite build + precompress)
_provenance.note: MEASURED by `node scripts/perf/app-weight.mjs --surface web --report` (#781, closing the #587 D21 web gap; re-measured and TIGHTENED by #883 C5). The earlier 'a weigh-in here would be a duplicate owner' claim was wrong: perf-budgets.ts shell.maxTransferBytes fences what the BROWSER transfers on the e2e shell journey (compressed, journey-scoped), not what the build ships on disk — the two can diverge by megabytes without either gate noticing the other's regression. Source maps plus the .br/.gz precompress sidecars (17.6 MB together) are excluded as diagnostics/alternate encodings of already-weighed bytes. THE DOUBLE-SHIPPED IROH WASM IS FIXED: the 1,995,618 B binding had two inclusion paths — the page's wasm-bindgen ESM resolving new URL('centraid_web_iroh_bg.wasm', import.meta.url) into a hashed assets/ copy, and scripts/build-iroh-worker.mjs copying the same bytes to public/centraid-worker-iroh.wasm for the CLASSIC service worker, which cannot import ESM. The worker's copy has to keep its unhashed, _headers-pinned path, so the centraid-iroh-wasm-single-copy plugin in apps/web/vite.config.ts rewrites the bindings' default to that same ?v=-stamped URL and the assets/ copy stops being emitted; public/sw.js now treats that path as an immutable shell entry, so a visit that uses both the page transport and the worker pays the 2 MB once. Measured on this host the same day: 10,074,585 B across 87 files before, 8,083,152 B across 86 files after. maxTotalBytes ratcheted 11,010,048 -> 8,730,000 (observed + ~8%). maxLargestChunkBytes is UNCHANGED at 2,200,000 deliberately: the largest single file is still that same 1,995,618 B binary — de-duplication removed a COPY, not weight from the copy that remains — so the existing observed+10% ceiling is still the honest one, and tightening it here would claim a win that did not happen. Next largest: pdf.worker.min.mjs 1.30 MB, boot.js 1.10 MB, sqlite3.wasm 865 kB; pdf.worker is the next real cut.
_provenance.headroom: observed + ~8% total; largest chunk + ~10% (mirrors the desktop/mobile seeds)
